current_source_behavior: Defaults/file/migration/overrides layering; no identity invalidation; known dict overrides accepted.
proposed_required_change: On every file import and inline-settings input, first validate the supplied metadata’s structure, recorded provenance constraints and requested_value binding against that supplied payload under its original setting names. A pre-existing stale, conflicting or malformed record is an input error, even if a later --set or GUI edit would remove it or make the value match. Preserve that original payload and work on a deep copy. Then perform proven one-to-one migration of the setting and its identity together, rejecting conflicting identities; overlay the migrated file onto defaults; coerce all explicit overrides and track every overridden model key; invalidate only the previously valid records for those keys, even if repeated overrides return to the old text; finally validate remaining/rebuilt bindings and module/backend compatibility. Apply this sequence to CLI, batch file/inline settings and GUI import. Rebuild only as a logged fresh exact trusted selection, never as repair of invalid imported evidence. Generic model_metadata --set replacement remains rejected.

current_source_behavior: Maps absolute string values recursively, including nested request binding; JSON serializes mapped settings.
proposed_required_change: Map ordinary settings using the existing path rule. Handle model_metadata as a reserved object: deep-copy each record and map only its requested_value with the same rule used for that record’s registered model setting. Never path-map key, version, version_status, sha256, kind or filename, even when their strings resemble absolute paths or expanded-home paths. Validate the original binding before mapping and the paired binding after mapping. Preserve the original exported payload separately; the mapped requested_value describes the effective mapped request. Paths outside the root and unsupported cross-platform paths remain unchanged; no Windows re-rooting guarantee is made.

current_source_behavior: Default/mixed version meaning; catalogue deduplicates key/name; nonblocking shared refresh can use network.
proposed_required_change: Preserve raw version declarations and conflicting rows for pure unique selection; explicit offline index, not remote=True block=False.

current_source_behavior: Missing separated paths refuse; exact first-match/fuzzy resolution; checksum downloads; no process coalescing.
proposed_required_change: Exact conjunct selector, pinned-local hashing, verified cache, strict policy and checked process lock. Before acquisition, pin the uniquely selected trusted current catalogue entry’s exact key, filename, kind and checksum. Copy a nonblank opaque version unchanged only when the trusted raw record explicitly declares it; otherwise record version_status=unspecified and version=null. Do not infer a release from ModelEntry.version=1 or filename/key/cache suffixes. Log that the legacy input supplied no historical identity and this choice identifies current catalogue bytes, not proven past laptop bytes. Any genuinely model-bound conflicting or ambiguous legacy version evidence still requires reconciliation. If the requested path is absent, offline cache reuse requires an exact complete identity match from the bounded trusted offline catalogue or a deliberately persisted trusted cache-provenance record, plus verification of the cached file’s checksum. A hash-only cached file without that trusted identity record does not establish catalogue-verified labels and must not silently satisfy this missing-path selector. Report the missing trusted metadata and exact copy requirements without any catalogue or weight traffic. The separate supplied-local-file route remains available: matching pinned bytes deliberately supplied at the effective requested path may be used with labels marked recorded rather than catalogue-verified, unless trusted available evidence contradicts them.

current_source_behavior: Multiple resolver seams and backend/sentinel/file-vs-directory meanings; no shared reserved metadata contract.
proposed_required_change: Use active module-specific model input registry; preserve scientific/backend checks after byte resolution.
